verdict.rationale: Antigravity's own agents work autonomously across editor, terminal and browser. They can hand test runs to subagents and produce review artifacts such as code diffs and browser recordings, which users can comment on, so build, test and demo for review is documented. The evidence never shows a cloud-hosted agent: execution runs in local desktop sessions and background worktrees, and Remote Control only drives sessions on your own machines. Missing for 10: cloud/remote-hosted agent execution, an explicit end-to-end demo workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have a cloud agent build, test, and demo a feature end-to-end for my review

citations.quote: Able to autonomously operate across your editor, terminal, and browser.
an agent can delegate tasks—such as running tests or performing extensive codebase searches—to dedicated subagents.
Artifacts include rich markdown plans (Implementation Plans), code diffs, architecture diagrams, images, and browser recordings.
Leave comments and feedback on any Artifact to better guide the Agent.
Projects natively support Git worktrees, allowing agents to operate in isolated background folders.
